title: The AI Revolution: Winners, Losers, & The Future of Tech | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 27

metadata.title: The AI Revolution: Winners, Losers, & The Future of Tech | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 27

summary: Dan Ives offers a broad AI bull case spanning identity, infrastructure, Apple distribution, Tesla autonomy, Palantir and small nuclear reactors. Eisman repeatedly probes adoption, operating proof, timing, interim earnings and China risk. Most precise operating visions extend to 2027-2032 and remain open; the xAI investment direction happened later than the specified November 2025 date. Important guest premises on European zero adoption and Palantir having no sales force are contradicted by primary evidence.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Dan Ives. Most specific technology and price forecasts are Ives; Eisman often questions rather than endorses them.
framework_points: Separate revolutionary technology from winners and losers.
Ask whether an incumbent moat protects renewals or merely historical profits.
Differentiate earnings forecasts from stock-price forecasts.
Demand operating and regulatory milestones for pre-revenue technology.
Identify how network utility actually accrues to token holders.
Trace second-order beneficiaries while checking their distinct economics.
tools_and_charts: AI capex and aggregate cash comparison
transcript_cautions: Publication is September 29, but discussion of the September 8 Eightco announcement as this week implies earlier recording; exact recording date not established.
Captions garble Eightco, Oklo, Palantir and decimal stock prices.
Perplexity/Google references appear confused; do not infer a verified ownership relationship.
Ives discloses chairmanship/ETF interests; promotional exposure is relevant context.
Guest forecasts are not Eisman forecasts.

assumptions: Share price reflects expected future cash flows and discount rates, not only current earnings.
The market can revise future-business value upward as near-term earnings decline.
evidence_basis.proof: A decline in current earnings can be offset in discounted equity value by a larger increase in expected later cash flows or lower discount rates. Thus an accurate earnings forecast does not logically guarantee a falling share price.
